changed.reason: Compactness alone does not ensure uniqueness of quadratic Kantorovich potentials. On a disconnected compact outcome support, independently shifting the dual constants on disconnected transport components gives multiple centered subgradients, and perturbing component masses produces a kink in the squared-Wasserstein functional. Connected regular support, together with the frozen positive densities, is the standard condition used by the verified first-variation theorem.

changed.from: \(\{I_{k,n}\}_{k=1}^K\) partitions \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). On \(\mathcal T_{-k,n}\), fit \(\widehat\pi_{-k,n}\) and a jointly measurable constrained conditional-density wavelet or sieve \(\widehat q_{a,-k,n}\in\Sigma(s,L;\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y)\) with \(c\le\widehat q_{a,-k,n}\le C\) and \(\int_{\mathcal Y}\widehat q_{a,-k,n}(x,y)d\ell_{\mathcal Y}(y)=1\) for every arm and almost every \(x\). Set \(\bar\pi_{-k,n}=\min\{1-\varepsilon,\max\{\varepsilon,\widehat\pi_{-k,n}\}\}\) and \(\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}(B\mid x)=\int_B\widehat q_{a,-k,n}(x,y)d\ell_{\mathcal Y}(y\).\) On compact \(\mathcal Y\), select the conditional quadratic optimizer and duals measurably by the minimum-norm normalized optimizer: \(x\mapsto\widehat\gamma_{-k,n}(\cdot\mid x)\) and \(x\mapsto(\widehat u_{0,-k,n},\widehat u_{1,-k,n})\). They obey \(\widehat u_{0,-k,n}(x,y_0)+\widehat u_{1,-k,n}(x,y_1)\le\lVert y_1-y_0\rVert_2^2\), equality \(\widehat\gamma_{-k,n}(\cdot\mid x)\)-almost everywhere, and \(\widehat V_{-k,n}(x)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int\widehat u_{a,-k,n}(x,y)\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}(dy\mid x)\). Define \(\widehat\phi_{a,-k,n}(x,y)=\widehat u_{a,-k,n}(x,y)-\int\widehat u_{a,-k,n}(x,z)\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}(dz\mid x)\), so \(\int\widehat\phi_{a,-k,n}(x,y)\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}(dy\mid x)=0\).
changed.to: Choose deterministic folds satisfying \(\max_{1\le k\le K}||I_{k,n}|-n/K|\le1\). Let \(\mathfrak F\) be the class of \(f\in\Sigma(s,L;\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y)\) such that \(c\le f\le C\) and \(\int_{\mathcal Y}f(x,y)d\ell_{\mathcal Y}(y)=1\) for almost every \(x\). Let \(\mathfrak F_{J_n}\) be a fixed finite \(L^\infty\)-net of \(\mathfrak F\), constructed by quantizing boundary-adapted tensor-wavelet coefficients through level \(J_n\), with mesh order \(2^{-J_ns}\) and logarithmic cardinality order \(2^{J_nD}\). Put \(N_{a,-k,n}=\sum_{j\notin I_{k,n}}1\{A_{j,n}=a\}\). If \(N_{a,-k,n}>0\), define \(\widehat q_{a,-k,n}\) as the lexicographically first minimizer over \(f\in\mathfrak F_{J_n}\) of \[\frac1{N_{a,-k,n}}\sum_{j\notin I_{k,n}:A_{j,n}=a}\left\{\int_{\mathcal Y}f(X_{j,n},y)^2d\ell_{\mathcal Y}(y)-2f(X_{j,n},Y_{j,n})\right\}.\] If \(N_{a,-k,n}=0\), use the first element of \(\mathfrak F_{J_n}\). Fit \(\widehat\pi_{-k,n}\) on the same training complement, set \(\bar\pi_{-k,n}=\min\{1-\varepsilon,\max\{\varepsilon,\widehat\pi_{-k,n}\}\}\), and define \(\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}(B\mid x)=\int_B\widehat q_{a,-k,n}(x,y)d\ell_{\mathcal Y}(y)\). Select the conditional quadratic optimizer and a mutually \(c\)-conjugate dual pair measurably by the minimum-norm normalized tie-break, obtaining \(x\mapsto\widehat\gamma_{-k,n}(\cdot\mid x)\) and \(x\mapsto(\widehat u_{0,-k,n},\widehat u_{1,-k,n})\). Require dual feasibility, contact on \(\widehat\gamma_{-k,n}\), and \(\widehat V_{-k,n}(x)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int\widehat u_{a,-k,n}(x,y)\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}(dy\mid x)\). Finally set \(\widehat\phi_{a,-k,n}=\widehat u_{a,-k,n}-\int\widehat u_{a,-k,n}d\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}\), so its fitted-kernel mean is exactly zero.
changed.reason: The frozen phrase ‘fit a wavelet or sieve’ does not define a sample map, and an arbitrary partition need not leave training samples of order \(n\). The proposed construction supplies balanced folds, an explicit conditional-density empirical-risk minimizer, a deterministic tie-break, normalization, and the same coupled OT objects used by the score.

changed.from: Use the constrained density learner in \(def:coupled-fold-learners\) at resolution \(2^{J_nD}\asymp n^{D/(2s+D)}\), balancing \(2^{-J_ns}\) and \((2^{J_nD}/n)^{1/2}\). Define \(r_{q,n}=n^{-s/(2s+D)}\), \(r_{\phi,n}=r_{q,n}\), \(r_{V,n}=r_{q,n}\), \(r_{S,n}=r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n}\), and \(r_{\sigma,n}=r_{S,n}+n^{-1/2}\). Require separately that the clipped propensity learner obey \(\max_k\lVert\bar\pi_{-k,n}-\pi_n\rVert_{L^2(P_{X,n})}=O_{P_n}(r_{\pi,n})\) with \(r_{\pi,n}=O(n^{-\beta})\).
changed.to:
Use the finite-net conditional-density empirical-risk minimizer in \(def:coupled-fold-learners\) with \(2^{J_nD}\asymp n^{D/(2s+D)}\). Define \(r_{q,n}=n^{-s/(2s+D)}\), \(r_{\phi,n}=r_{q,n}\), \(r_{V,n}=r_{q,n}\), \(r_{S,n}=r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n}\), and \(r_{\sigma,n}=r_{S,n}+n^{-1/2}\). The density rate is to be derived from the approximation bound \(2^{-J_ns}\), the entropy bound \(\log|\mathfrak F_{J_n}|\lesssim2^{J_nD}\), and the empirical conditional-density loss. Separately require the uniform clipped-propensity condition
\[\lim_{M\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}}P_n\!\left(\max_k\lVert\bar\pi_{-k,n}-\pi_n\rVert_{L^2(P_{X,n})}>Mr_{\pi,n}\right)=0,\qquad r_{\pi,n}=O(n^{-\beta}).\]

changed.reason: Pointwise \(O_{P_n}\) control cannot imply the theorem's supremum-over-laws conclusion. The corrected route states the exact uniform propensity condition and makes clear which rates are definitions and which remain mathematical consequences.

changed.to: \(\mathcal X\) is the closure of a bounded connected Lipschitz domain in \(\mathbb R^{d_X}\), and \(\mathcal Y\) is the closure of a bounded connected uniformly convex \(C^2\) domain with nonempty interior in \(\mathbb R^{d_Y}\).
changed.reason: Connectedness is needed for uniqueness of centered quadratic dual potentials and hence for the canonical gradient. Lipschitz and uniformly convex regular geometry supplies the extension, Poincare, and boundary regularity used by the conditional-density and Brenier arguments.

changed.to: Let \(\mathfrak F\) be the feasible conditional-density class in the corrected \(def:coupled-fold-learners\). There exist fixed constants \(0<m_{\mathrm{OT}}\le M_{\mathrm{OT}}<\infty\) such that, for every \(f_0,f_1\in\mathfrak F\) and almost every \(x\), the quadratic Brenier potential \(b_{f_0,f_1,x}\) transporting \(f_0(x,\cdot)\) to \(f_1(x,\cdot)\) belongs to \(C^2(\mathcal Y)\) and satisfies \[m_{\mathrm{OT}}I_{d_Y}\preceq\nabla_y^2b_{f_0,f_1,x}(y)\preceq M_{\mathrm{OT}}I_{d_Y}\quad\text{for every }y\in\mathcal Y.\]
changed.reason: The frozen strong-convexity condition concerns only one selected true potential and supplies no upper curvature bound or fitted-pair regularity. The score uses fitted potentials, so the reverse quadratic expansion and centered-potential stability require uniform two-sided curvature for every feasible fitted pair.

changed.reason: The current full-class statement is too strong and, as a uniform learner theorem, vacuous: \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\) restricts the propensity only by overlap, so it contains arbitrary measurable propensities. An unseen-covariate-cell construction leaves a fixed positive fraction of propensity bits unobserved and prevents any learner from having a uniform \(L^2(P_{X,n})\) rate \(O(n^{-\beta})\) with \(\beta>0\) over that class. In addition, the asserted quadratic transport remainder and potential stability require the already-frozen support-geometry and all-feasible-pairs curvature assumptions, neither of which is a current theorem hypothesis. The proposed claim preserves the estimand, estimator, rate conditions, asymptotic linearity, efficiency, studentized limit, and coverage conclusion, but restricts uniformity to a declared nonempty law subclass on which a fixed measurable propensity rule actually attains the stated rate and explicitly imposes the two transport assumptions.

Let \(h=g-f\), so \(\int h=0\). Solve the weak Neumann problem

\[
\int_{\mathcal Y}\nabla\varphi\cdot\nabla\eta
=
\int_{\mathcal Y}h\eta,
\qquad \eta\in H^1(\mathcal Y),
\]

with \(\int\varphi=0\). Poincaré and Lax–Milgram give

\[
\|\nabla\varphi\|_2\le C_{\mathcal Y}\|h\|_2.
\]

Set

\[
\rho_t=(1-t)f+tg,\qquad
j_t=\nabla\varphi,\qquad
v_t=\frac{j_t}{\rho_t}.
\]

\[
\int_0^1\int_{\mathcal Y}\frac{|j_t|^2}{\rho_t}
\le
c^{-1}C_{\mathcal Y}^2\|f-g\|_2^2.

\(\zeta\in C_c^\infty((0,1)\times\mathbb R^{d_Y})\), extending \(\rho_t\) and \(j_t\) by zero outside \(\mathcal Y\),

\[
\int_0^1\int
\{\rho_t\partial_t\zeta+j_t\cdot\nabla\zeta\}=0.
\]

The weak Neumann formulation supplies the zero normal trace required for the zero extension. Therefore \((\rho_t,j_t)\) is a Benamou–Brenier admissible curve; no classical flow is required. The dynamic formula yields

\[
W_2^2(f\,dy,g\,dy)
\le
c^{-1}C_{\mathcal Y}^2\|f-g\|_2^2.

\[
S_{\widehat P,\widehat Q}(b)
=
\int b\,d\widehat P+\int b^*\,d\widehat Q,
\qquad
\Delta=S_{\widehat P,\widehat Q}(b)
-\min_{\widetilde b}S_{\widehat P,\widehat Q}(\widetilde b).

\[
\Delta
=
\int
\{b(\xi)+b^*(\zeta)-\langle\xi,\zeta\rangle\}
\,d\widehat\gamma.
\]

Since \(b^*\) is \(M_{\mathrm{OT}}^{-1}\)-strongly convex and

\[
\Delta
\ge
\frac1{2M_{\mathrm{OT}}}
\int|\zeta-T(\xi)|^2\,d\widehat\gamma.

=
S(b)-E_{\widehat\gamma}\langle U,V\rangle
\le
S(b)-E_\eta\langle U,V\rangle.

\[
b(U)+b^*(V)-\langle U,V\rangle
\le
\frac{M_{\mathrm{OT}}}{2}|U-X|^2
+
\frac1{2m_{\mathrm{OT}}}|V-Y|^2
-
\langle U-X,V-Y\rangle.

\[
\Delta
\le
\frac{M_{\mathrm{OT}}}{2}W_2^2(P,\widehat P)
+
\frac1{2m_{\mathrm{OT}}}W_2^2(Q,\widehat Q)
+
W_2(P,\widehat P)W_2(Q,\widehat Q).

changed.to:
Theorem 2 (conditional observational DML for the sharp COT endpoint). Fix the predetermined triangular law class \(\mathscr P\) in \(def:predetermined-triangular-law-class\). Use the normalized coupled learners in \(def:coupled-fold-learners\), the density route in \(def:foldwise-rate-route\), and a predetermined propensity learner satisfying the generic uniform rate condition in \(def:propensity-rate-regimes\) for a deterministic \(r_{\pi,n}\to0\). Suppose
\[
r_{q,n}^2=o(n^{-1/2}),\qquad r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n}=o(n^{-1/2}),\qquad r_{\pi,n}+r_{q,n}=o(1).
\]
Then, uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathscr P\), the exact fold bias is
\[
\mathcal B_{k,n}=-E_{P_{X,n}}\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OT}}(Q,\widehat Q)
+E_{P_{X,n}}\sum_a\left(\frac{\pi_{a,n}}{\bar\pi_{a,-k,n}}-1\right)
\int\widehat\phi_{a,-k,n}\,d(Q_{a,P_n}-\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}),
\]
where \(\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OT}}\ge0\). Its two terms have orders \(O_{P_n}(r_{q,n}^2)\) and \(O_{P_n}(r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n})\). Moreover,
\[
\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_n(O_{i,n})+R_n,
\quad
R_n=O_{P_n}(r_{q,n}^2+r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n}+n^{-1/2}(r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n}))=o_{P_n}(n^{-1/2}),
\]
\[
\widehat\sigma_n^2-\sigma_n^2=O_{P_n}(r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n}+n^{-1/2})=o_{P_n}(1),
\]
and
\[
\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathscr P}\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}
\left|P_n\!\left(\frac{\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n)}{\widehat\sigma_n}\le t\right)-\Phi(t)\right|\to0.
\]
Also \(\widehat\sigma_n/\sigma_n\to1\) uniformly in probability, \(\inf_{\mathbf P\in\mathscr P}P_n(\widehat\sigma_n>0)\to1\), and the two-sided Wald interval has uniform asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\). Its leading variance is the efficiency bound \(\sigma_n^2\).

A centered Gaussian spectral calibration for a second-order Hessian exists in \\(L^2\\) exactly when its eigenvalues are square summable, and uniform finite-rank calibration requires a uniform square-summable tail. {"id":"lem:uniform-studentized-limit","kind":"lemma","statement":"Let \(\mathscr C\subseteq\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs}}_{\sigma_\star}\) be predetermined.  Suppose, uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathscr C\), that \(O_{1,n},\ldots,O_{n,n}\) are i.i.d., \(E_{P_n}[\psi_n]=0\), \(|\psi_n|\le M\), and
\[
\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_n(O_{i,n})+o_{P_n}(n^{-1/2}),\qquad
\widehat\sigma_n^2-\sigma_n^2=o_{P_n}(1).
\]
Then the studentized statistic converges to \(N(0,1)\) uniformly over \(\mathscr C\) in Kolmogorov distance, \(\widehat\sigma_n/\sigma_n\to1\) uniformly, \(\inf_{\mathbf P\in\mathscr C}P_n(\widehat\sigma_n>0)\to1\), and the associated two-sided Wald interval has uniform asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\).","depends_on":["ass:observed-iid","ass:variance-separated","def:empirical-studentizer","lem:uniform-bounded-triangular-clt","lem:cross-fit-remainder-variance"],"status":"to-prove"}

note: D0.5 revise findings + codex maximality IMPROVE
directive:
D0.5 RETURNED REVISE AND THE MAXIMALITY CONSULT RETURNED IMPROVE. Perform one coordinated bounded revision covering all six targets below. Preserve every sound proof; re-derive only what these changes touch.

(1) SCOPE REPAIR lem:two-sample-map-stability. The statement currently quantifies over arbitrary feasible P,Q,hatP,hatQ, but the curvature premise and the reproduced proof only cover pairs in the all-feasible density class F. Narrow the statement and add the hypotheses explicitly: fix x in the common full-measure set; require P,Q,hatP,hatQ to be probability laws on Y whose densities are x-sections of elements of F (hence the common bounds c <= f <= C, normalization, and Holder feasibility); require Y convex and the Brenier potential b from P to Q to be C^2 with m_OT * I <= Hess(b) <= M_OT * I; for the reverse assertion impose the same all-feasible-pairs conditions after swapping marginals; let hatgamma in Gamma(hatP,hatQ) be optimal. This is a FAITHFUL narrowing toward truth, not a weaken-to-prove: the truth lies in F by the model assumptions and every fitted density lies in F_{J_n} subset F by construction.

(2) SCOPE REPAIR lem:two-sample-quadratic-remainder. Same defect, same remedy. Require every component of barP=(barP_0,barP_1) and P=(P_0,P_1) to have a density that is an x-section of an element of F; require the common bounds c <= f <= C, normalization, convex support Y, and the uniform C^2, lower-curvature and upper-curvature assumptions for every ordered pair generated by these four densities; let (baru_0,baru_1) be a mutually conjugate optimal dual pair at barP. State that C_OT depends only on the common class constants and support geometry.

After (1) and (2), verify every downstream consumer still goes through unchanged: lem:conditional-transport-stability-rates, lem:assignment-score-rates, lem:cross-fit-remainder-variance, thm:regular-efficient-inference. If any consumer genuinely breaks, report it rather than silently re-scoping the consumer.

(3) COMPARATOR thm:regular-efficient-inference. The field-tier novelty claim is not yet supported because the closest smooth-Wasserstein efficiency result is cited only for stability. Add an explicit comparator separating the two: Manole et al. (2024) derive influence functions, local asymptotic minimax bounds, and efficient plug-in inference for the UNCONDITIONAL one- and two-sample functional W_2^2(P,Q) from independent marginal samples; the present theorem treats covariate-indexed CONDITIONAL marginals integrated over an unknown covariate law in ONE OBSERVATIONAL sample, whose observed-data canonical gradient carries the additional V(X)-theta term and inverse-propensity-weighted arm derivatives, and establishes propensity-corrected cross-fitted uniform studentization and Wald coverage.

(4) STRENGTHEN THE HEADLINE thm:regular-efficient-inference: promote the proved vanishing-variance regime. The theorem is currently uniform only over the fixed variance-separated class sigma_n >= sigma_star > 0, but the relative conditions sqrt(n)*delta_n/sigma_n -> 0, eta_n/sigma_n^2 -> 0 and sqrt(n)*sigma_n -> infinity are ALREADY PROVED and cover positive vanishing variance. Restate the headline over that wider regime. Do NOT claim Gaussian coverage at exact equality: the degeneracy theorem governs there.

(5) GENERALITY thm:observed-gradient. State the canonical-gradient/efficiency-bound result at its true generality: it needs overlap, square-integrability, and conditional-OT pathwise differentiability with unique normalized potentials. Consistency and ignorability are required only for the CAUSAL IDENTIFICATION step, and the Holder classes and all-feasible-pairs curvature conditions are estimator-side sufficient conditions, not preconditions for the gradient. Separate the identification hypotheses from the gradient hypotheses rather than carrying all of them on the gradient statement.

(6) DEMOTE OVER-CLAIMS. In prop:holder-propensity-efficient-inference, do not present s > D/2 or t_pi > D*d_X/(4s) as sharp: they are sufficient thresholds induced by L2-density rates and a first-order remainder, and a conditional H^{-1}/Wasserstein-rate analysis could improve the transport remainder. Either prove matching minimax lower bounds or label both thresholds explicitly proof-route-specific. In thm:degeneracy-frontier-and-spectral-obstruction, keep the claim as an obstruction to the unregularized full-tangent spectral route, not a general impossibility; where it is reachable, extend the noncompactness argument beyond the special constant-density pi=1/2 equality law to general nonatomic-P_X equality laws admitting a nonzero admissible outcome direction.

(7) SYNC THE PROSE FIELDS. Item (4) changes the headline regime and items (5)-(6) change positioning, so update tldr, project_justification.gap, project_justification.niche, project_justification.fill and related_work to match the new headline and the Manole comparator. The change-apply loop has no prose channel and RENDER emits prose verbatim, so stale prose would ship as an over-claim.

Theorem 2 (conditional observational DML for the sharp COT endpoint with positive vanishing variance). Let \(\mathscr C\subseteq\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vu}}\) be any predetermined collection such that \(\sigma_n>0\) for every row law under consideration; exact equality is excluded. Use the predetermined normalized coupled learners in \(\texttt{def:coupled-fold-learners}\) and suppose their displayed uniform conditional-density rate premise holds over \(\mathscr C\). Use a predetermined propensity learner satisfying the generic uniform \(L^2(P_{X,n})\) rate premise in \(\texttt{def:propensity-rate-regimes}\) over \(\mathscr C\), for deterministic \(r_{\pi,n}\to0\). Define
\[\delta_n=r_{q,n}^2+r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n}+n^{-1/2}(r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n}),\qquad \eta_n=r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n}+n^{-1/2}.\]
Suppose, uniformly over \(\mathscr C\),
\[\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathscr C}\frac{\sqrt n\,\delta_n}{\sigma_n}\to0,\qquad \sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathscr C}\frac{\eta_n}{\sigma_n^2}\to0,\qquad \inf_{\mathbf P\in\mathscr C}\sqrt n\,\sigma_n\to\infty.\]
Then the exact fold bias is
\[\mathcal B_{k,n}=-E_{P_{X,n}}\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OT}}(Q,\widehat Q)+E_{P_{X,n}}\sum_a\left(\frac{\pi_{a,n}}{\bar\pi_{a,-k,n}}-1\right)\int\widehat\phi_{a,-k,n}\,d(Q_{a,P_n}-\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}),\]
where \(\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OT}}\ge0\), and its terms are \(O_{P_n}(r_{q,n}^2)\) and \(O_{P_n}(r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n})\). Moreover,
\[\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_n(O_{i,n})+R_n,\qquad R_n=O_{P_n}(\delta_n)=o_{P_n}(\sigma_n/\sqrt n),\]
\[\widehat\sigma_n^2-\sigma_n^2=O_{P_n}(\eta_n)=o_{P_n}(\sigma_n^2),\]
and the studentized statistic converges uniformly to \(N(0,1)\) in Kolmogorov distance. Also \(\widehat\sigma_n/\sigma_n\to1\) uniformly, \(\inf_{\mathbf P\in\mathscr C}P_n(\widehat\sigma_n>0)\to1\), and the two-sided Wald interval has uniform asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\). The influence function is the observed-data canonical gradient \(\psi_n\), so the leading variance attains the semiparametric efficiency bound. Unlike the unconditional one- or two-marginal-sample result summarized in \(\texttt{lem:manole-unconditional-smooth-wasserstein-efficiency}\), this single observational-sample theorem includes the covariate-composition and inverse-propensity terms in \(\psi_n\).

Exact equality remains excluded.

The abstract theorem's hypothesis D(P_n) (conditional-transport pathwise differentiability) quantifies over EVERY regular dominated one-dimensional submodel, but lem:integrated-arm-path-differentiation establishes the derivative only for submodels with FIXED SUPPORT and overlap in a neighborhood of zero. note: D0-MAXIMALITY IMPROVE (codex gpt-5.6-sol medium): 5 honest strengthenings + prose sync
directive:
D0-MAXIMALITY IMPROVE. The paper is fully discharged, but a whole-paper maximization review found five
honest strengthenings that the EXISTING arguments already support. None requires a new assumption. Do NOT
strengthen any structural assumption to obtain these, and do NOT weaken any existing conclusion. Preserve
every sound proof; extend rather than restart.

(1) SHARPEN THE EMPIRICAL-VARIANCE ANALYSIS — the load-bearing one.
Nodes: lem:cross-fit-remainder-variance, lem:vanishing-variance-studentization, thm:regular-efficient-inference.
The current variance bound discards the shrinking scale of psi_n and reads
  hat-sigma_n^2 - sigma_n^2 = O_P(r_{S,n} + n^{-1/2}).
Replace it by the scale-aware bound
  O_P( sigma_n r_{S,n} + r_{S,n}^2 + (sigma_n + r_{S,n}) / sqrt(n) ).
Derive it using P psi_n^2 = sigma_n^2, Cauchy-Schwarz |P(psi_n Delta_{k,n})| <= sigma_n ||Delta_{k,n}||_2,
and Var(psi_n^2) <~ sigma_n^2, instead of the uniform envelope alone. Then WEAKEN the near-degeneracy
requirement accordingly: replace the condition eta_n / sigma_n^2 -> 0 by the pair
  r_{S,n} / sigma_n -> 0   and   sqrt(n) sigma_n -> infinity.
This enlarges the proved positive-variance region from roughly r_{S,n} = o(sigma_n^2) to r_{S,n} = o(sigma_n).
Propagate the weakened condition everywhere it is invoked.

(2) STATE THE VANISHING-VARIANCE PHASE BOUNDARY EXPLICITLY.
Node: prop:holder-propensity-efficient-inference.
With a_q = s/(2s+D), a_pi = t_pi/(2 t_pi + d_X), and sigma_n asymptotically n^{-kappa}, record that the
sharpened theorem applies whenever
  kappa < min{ 2 a_q - 1/2,  a_pi + a_q - 1/2,  a_q,  a_pi,  1/2 }.
For the known-propensity case, drop the a_pi-dependent terms. This is a direct substitution into the proved
remainder and the sharpened variance condition from (1); it surfaces an elbow the note currently hides.

(3) SPLIT IDENTIFICATION FROM EFFICIENCY UNDER MINIMAL HYPOTHESES.
Node: thm:observed-gradient.
The identification clause currently carries fixed epsilon-overlap and ass:regular-support-geometry, but its
proof needs only consistency, conditional ignorability, and arm positivity P{pi_a(X) > 0} = 1 for a = 0,1.
State the identification clause under exactly those. State the efficiency clause via the primitive analytic
properties U(P_n), D(P_n), G(P_n) already established in thm:abstract-observed-canonical-gradient, and

changed.from: Theorem (degeneracy frontier and obstruction to the unregularized full-tangent spectral route).  Let \(P_n\) be a row law of the variance-unrestricted parent \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vu}}\), equivalently \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\) satisfying \(ass:regular-support-geometry\) and the three all-feasible-pairs conditional Brenier conditions.  Then \(\sigma_n^2=0\) if and only if \(Q_{0,P_n}(\cdot\mid x)=Q_{1,P_n}(\cdot\mid x)\) for \(P_{X,n}\)-almost every \(x\).  At equality, \(\theta_n=0\), \(\psi_n=0\), and the oracle first-order Gaussian pivot has Kolmogorov distance \(1/2\) from \(N(0,1)\).  Along every smooth equality path described in \(\texttt{lem:equality-degeneracy-and-second-variation}\), the second directional derivative is the displayed weighted Neumann energy.  A centered Gaussian spectral calibration for a second-order Hessian exists in \(L^2\) exactly when its eigenvalues are square summable, and uniform finite-rank calibration requires a uniform square-summable tail.  The parent class does not imply this condition: whenever it contains the equality law in \(\texttt{lem:conditional-hessian-spectral-obstruction}\) with nonatomic \(P_X\), the conditional Hessian has an infinite-dimensional compression equal to a positive multiple of the identity and is neither compact nor Hilbert--Schmidt.  Consequently, the unregularized \(n\)-scale full-tangent spectral/Gaussian route named in \(\texttt{def:degeneracy-handle}\) cannot yield a uniformly tight equality calibration over \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vu}}\).  A positive theorem using that route must impose or construct covariate-direction regularization, a uniform Hilbert--Schmidt tail, and uniform estimation of the regularized Hessian.  On collections with \(\sigma_n>0\), the first-order studentized limit remains uniformly valid under the relative-rate conditions in \(\texttt{lem:vanishing-variance-studentization}\).  This is a route-specific negative result and does not rule out slower regularized or other derivative-aware confidence procedures; honest degeneracy-adaptive inference over the entire parent remains open.

changed.from:
{"id":"lem:vanishing-variance-studentization","kind":"lemma","statement":"Consider any collection of i.i.d. triangular sequences in the variance-unrestricted parent class with \(\sigma_n>0\), \(E[\psi_n]=0\), and \(|\psi_n|\le M_\psi\). Suppose, uniformly over that collection,
\[
\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_n(O_{i,n})+O_{P_n}(\delta_n),\qquad
\widehat\sigma_n^2-\sigma_n^2=O_{P_n}(\eta_n),
\]
where
\[
\frac{\sqrt n\,\delta_n}{\sigma_n}\to0,\qquad
\frac{\eta_n}{\sigma_n^2}\to0,\qquad
\sqrt n\,\sigma_n\to\infty
\]
uniformly. Then
\[
\sup_P\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\left|P_n\!\left(\frac{\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n)}{\widehat\sigma_n}\le t\right)-\Phi(t)\right|\to0,
\]
\(\widehat\sigma_n/\sigma_n\to1\) uniformly in probability, and the associated Wald intervals have uniform asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\). For the frozen one-step decomposition one may take \(\delta_n=r_{q,n}^2+r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n}+n^{-1/2}(r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n})\) and \(\eta_n=r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n}+n^{-1/2}\), whenever its remainder conclusions hold uniformly on the sequence collection.","depends_on":["ass:observed-iid","def:foldwise-rate-route","def:one-step-estimator","def:empirical-studentizer"],"status":"proved","proof_tex":"Write
\[
Z_n=\frac1{\sigma_n\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_n(O_{i,n}).
\]
For fixed \(t\), Taylor's formula for the complex exponential, \(E[\psi_n]=0\), and \(E[\psi_n^2]=\sigma_n^2\) give
\[
E\exp\left(\frac{it\psi_n}{\sigma_n\sqrt n}\right)
=1-\frac{t^2}{2n}+\rho_n(t),
\]
where
\[
|\rho_n(t)|\le\frac{|t|^3E|\psi_n|^3}{6\sigma_n^3n^{3/2}}
\le\frac{|t|^3M_\psi}{6\sigma_n n^{3/2}}. \tag{1}
\]
The second inequality uses \(|\psi_n|^3\le M_\psi\psi_n^2\). Since \(\sqrt n\,\sigma_n\to\infty\), multiplying the last bound in (1) by \(n\) gives a quantity tending uniformly to zero. Independence within rows therefore yields
\[
E[e^{itZ_n}]
=\left\{1-\frac{t^2}{2n}+\rho_n(t)\right\}^n
\longrightarrow e^{-t^2/2}. \tag{2}
\]
The convergence is uniform over the stated collection. A subsequence argument turns (2) into uniform Kolmogorov convergence: if uniform convergence of distribution functions failed, choose a violating sequence of laws; (2) along that sequence gives weak convergence to the continuous standard-normal distribution, which implies convergence in Kolmogorov distance, a contradiction. Thus
\[
\sup_P\sup_t|P_n(Z_n\le t)-\Phi(t)|\to0. \tag{3}
\]

The variance condition and positivity of \(\sigma_n\) give
\[
\left|\frac{\widehat\sigma_n}{\sigma_n}-1\right|
=\frac{|\widehat\sigma_n^2-\sigma_n^2|}{\sigma_n(\widehat\sigma_n+\sigma_n)}
\le\frac{|\widehat\sigma_n^2-\sigma_n^2|}{\sigma_n^2}
=o_{P_n}(1) \tag{4}
\]
uniformly. In particular, \(P_n(\widehat\sigma_n>0)\to1\) uniformly. If \(R_n\) denotes the estimator remainder, the first relative-rate condition gives
\[
\frac{\sqrt nR_n}{\sigma_n}=o_{P_n}(1). \tag{5}
\]
On the event of a positive denominator, the studentized statistic equals
\[
\frac{Z_n+\sqrt nR_n/\sigma_n}{\widehat\sigma_n/\sigma_n}.
\]
Equations (3)--(5), using the same subsequence argument for uniformity, prove the asserted uniform standard-normal limit. The frozen zero-denominator convention changes the statistic only on an event of uniformly vanishing probability. Evaluating the limit at \(\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\) gives
\[
P_n\!\left(\theta_n\in\left[\widehat\theta_n\mathbin\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\widehat\sigma_n/\sqrt n\right]\right)\to1-\alpha
\]
uniformly. If the stated one-step remainder and variance bounds hold, the final assertion follows by substituting their deterministic upper envelopes into the two relative-rate conditions."}

\[

Conditional on \(\mathcal T_{-k,n}\), this is a fixed measurable function and the observations in \(I_{k,n}\) are independent with law \(P_n\). Conditioning successively on \(X_n\) and \(A_n\) gives
\[
P_n\widehat S_{-k,n}=E_{P_{X,n}}\!\left[\widehat V_{-k,n}+\sum_a\frac{\pi_{a,n}}{\bar\pi_{a,-k,n}}\int\widehat\phi_{a,-k,n}\,dQ_{a,P_n}\right].

Because \(\int\widehat\phi_{a,-k,n}d\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}=0\), adding and subtracting the fitted kernel and writing \(\pi_a/\bar\pi_a=1+(\pi_a/\bar\pi_a-1)\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}

={}&E_{P_{X,n}}\!\left[\widehat V_{-k,n}-V_n+\sum_a\int\widehat\phi_{a,-k,n}d(Q_{a,P_n}-\widehat Q_{a,-k,n})\right]\\

\end{aligned}
\]

The final identity in \(\texttt{lem:conditional-transport-stability-rates}\) proves the exact fold-bias formula and the nonpositive \(O_{P_n}(r_{q,n}^2)\) order of its first term. The first assertion of \(\texttt{lem:assignment-score-rates}\) gives \(O_{P_n}(r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n})\) for the second.

\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n
&=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_n(O_{i,n})+\sum_k w_{k,n}\mathbb P_{k,n}\Delta_{k,n}\\
&=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_n(O_{i,n})+\sum_k w_{k,n}\mathcal B_{k,n}+\sum_k w_{k,n}(\mathbb P_{k,n}-P_n)\Delta_{k,n}.
\end{aligned} \tag{1}
\]
Conditionally on the training sample,
\[
E\!\left[\{(\mathbb P_{k,n}-P_n)\Delta_{k,n}\}^2\mid\mathcal T_{-k,n}\right]\le\frac{P_n\Delta_{k,n}^2}{m_{k,n}}.
\]

\[
\sum_k w_{k,n}(\mathbb P_{k,n}-P_n)\Delta_{k,n}=O_{P_n}(n^{-1/2}r_{S,n}). \tag{2}
\]

\[

\[

\[
\widehat\sigma_n^2-\sigma_n^2=O_{P_n}(r_{S,n}+n^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathscr C\)."}
